Subject: Realtime inference errors & throughput collapse — urgent

Kim,

We're seeing a sudden spike in 5xxs and token latency across our production app starting ~07:05 PST. Error rate is ~18% on /v1/generate and p50 latency jumped from ~180ms to >1.2s. Throughput dropped by ~60% and customers are reporting timeouts.

Attached is a small sample of request/response pairs and our front-end logs. Key notes:
- Errors are predominantly 502/504 from the inference endpoint.
- Spike corresponds with heavy daytime burst on our west coast users.
- We rely on your hosted endpoint in us-west-2 and have no local fallback.

Please escalate — we need an immediate mitigation plan and timeline. Our incident ops is standing by, cc'd.

Thanks,
Alex Lopez
Director of Platform Engineering
HealthWorks

Quick findings from telemetry and traces (first pass):
- Root symptom: KV cache saturation on us-west-2a nodes; high KV cache miss penalty coincident with continuous batching delays.
- Queue backlog: front-end queues in the serving tier spiked, leading to head-of-line latency.
- Error profile: 502/504s originate at the gateway layer when downstream serving jobs exceed queue window; no immediate OOMs observed but GPU utilization is uneven.

Short mitigations we can do now (20–45m):
1) Reroute 35–45% of traffic from us-west-2 to us-west-1 (compatible model variant available) — expected immediate p50 improvement.
2) Temporarily lower batch size and enable aggressive KV eviction for HealthWorks' tenant to reduce per-request latency (small quality risk).
3) Open burst capacity on the reserved Dedicated pool (may need ops to approve burst credit).

I attached a Prometheus snippet and a heatmap export. If we reroute, we should enable prefix caching in us-west-1 and monitor for tail latency.

(attachment: prometheus-snip.txt)

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-12-09T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: Escalation: HealthWorks P0 — request board notification

Team — summary for execs and board notification request:

What happened: sudden throughput collapse and elevated 5xxs for HealthWorks (hosted in us-west-2). Initial telemetry points to KV cache saturation in us-west-2a causing queue amplification and gateway 502s.

Immediate plan (we executed parts of this already):
- Rerouted 40% of traffic to us-west-1 compatible variant (live at 08:55).
- Lowered batch size for HealthWorks' tenant and enabled aggressive KV eviction (deployed 08:58).
- Opened burst capacity request to Dedicated operations; Marcus is validating node availability.

Impact: p50 is down ~140ms from the spike, error rate dropped to ~4% (still above baseline). Remaining risk: cross-region tail latency and potential capacity exhaust if surge continues.

Ask: approval to notify board & apply a one-time service credit (provisional) to HealthWorks given P0 customer impact. Also request Sean to prepare a short triage note for the board (one slide) and for Legal to hold on possible SLA credit wording.

I'll coordinate a 30-min bridge in 15m for final decisions.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: HealthWorks incident update — mitigation steps and next actions

Alex / HealthWorks team —

Thank you for the quick signals and for sending logs. We ran an emergency mitigation and wanted to confirm what we've done and the next steps:

What we did (completed):
- Rerouted ~40% of HealthWorks production traffic from us-west-2 to us-west-1 at 08:55 PST to reduce pressure on the saturated AZ.
- Lowered batch size and enabled aggressive KV eviction for HealthWorks' tenant at 08:58 PST to reduce queuing latency.
- Opened burst capacity and validated additional Dedicated nodes — Marcus confirmed capacity available at 09:20 PST.

Immediate impact: error rate reduced from ~18% to ~3.8%, p50 latency recovered toward baseline (~200ms). We continue to monitor tail latency and cross-region variance.

Next steps:
- Detailed post-incident analysis (postmortem) will be published within 72 hours.
- We're preparing a one-time credit proposal for HealthWorks while we investigate root cause and long-term mitigations.
- Suggested follow-ups: KV cache tuning, model quantization recommendation for HealthWorks' heavy tail traffic, and an optional dedicated routing pin to avoid AZ mixing during peak windows.

Attachments: timeline-snapshot.pdf (initial timeline), logs_20261209.zip (raw sample).

We apologize for the disruption. Please let us know if you'd like a bridge now or a walk-through of the mitigation steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability & Success
Redwood Inference
